newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: At least 10 killed in Colombia violence.
newsitem.headline: At least 10 killed in Colombia violence.

text.p: At least 10 people were killed in the latest round of political violence across Colombia, including six who were shot dead by hooded gunmen in a coal-mining district of northwest Antioquia province, authorities said on Saturday.

The victims included two policemen who were killed shortly before dawn when leftist Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels stormed a highway toll booth outside the city of Villavicencio, about 40 miles (65 km) southeast of Bogota, and reduced it to rubble with dynamite.

Police and military officials said the worst attack occurred late on Friday in the municipality of Vegachi, where a group of about 20 hooded gunmen killed six people and abducted at least five others who they carried off in the back of a truck.
National radio reports, which could not be immediately confirmed, said as many as 12 people were dragged off by the gumen who belonged to a suspected right-wing death squad operating in the area.
In the nearby town of Yali, at least two people were killed and two policemen wounded in an attack on Friday by leftist National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrillas, army spokesmen said.

Authorities say the FARC and ELN, both founded in the mid- 1960s and Latin America's largest and longest-lasting insurgency, have a combined force of about 12,000 guerrillas who operate throughout Colombia.
